title: Get started as a Solution Partner
snippet:
| Asset | Specific Instructions |
|---|---|
| **Business portfolio** | You can use an existing one, or [set up a new one⁠](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1710077379203657). Save the business portfolio ID. |
| **WhatsApp Business account** (WABA) | See [Create a WhatsApp Business account for the WhatsApp Business API⁠](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2087193751603668) for help. |
| [**Meta App**](/apps/) | If you don’t have an app, you need to [create one](/docs/development/create-an-app) with the **Business** type. Remember to add a display name and a contact email to your app. As a Solution Partner, your app must go through [App Review](/docs/app-review) and request **Advanced access** to the following permissions: - [`whatsapp_business_management`](/docs/permissions/reference/whatsapp_business_management) — Manage phone numbers, message templates, registration, and business profiles under a WhatsApp Business account. If your app uses this permission to access WABAs not owned by your business, you must have **Advanced access**. Without it, API calls return error code `200`. To get **Advanced access**, submit your app for [App Review](/docs/app-review). - [`whatsapp_business_messaging`](/docs/permissions/reference/whatsapp_business_messaging) — Used to send/receive messages from WhatsApp users, upload/download media under a WhatsApp Business account. To get this permission, your app must go through [App Review](/docs/app-review). - [`whatsapp_business_manage_events`](/docs/permissions#whatsapp_business_manage_events) — Used to log events — such as purchases, add-to-cart actions, leads, and more under a WhatsApp Business account. Only request this permission if you are using the [Marketing Messages API for WhatsApp](/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/marketing-messages/overview) with [Conversions API](/documentation/ads-commerce/conversions-api). To get this permission, your app must go through [App Review](/docs/app-review).

In order to access the WhatsApp Business Messaging Cloud API you need to first accept the WhatsApp Business Platform Terms of Service on behalf of your business.

title: Partners | Meta for Developers
snippet:
Partners are business entities that deploy value-added solutions as WhatsApp authorized service providers on behalf of their clients. Partners include Solution Partners, Tech Providers, and Tech Partners.
## Solution Partners
Solution Partners are [Meta Business Partners⁠](https://www.facebook.com/business/marketing-partners/become-a-partner) that provide a full range of WhatsApp Business Platform services to other businesses (clients), such as messaging services, billing, integration support, and customer support.
Solution Partners have [credit lines⁠](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1684730811624773?id=2129163877102343) which can be extended to clients who they bring on board, thus removing the need for those clients to enter their own payment method during the onboarding process. Furthermore, Solution Partners can directly invoice their clients for the WhatsApp Business Platform services provided through their apps.

Tech Providers are similar to Solution Partners in that they also can offer a full range of WhatsApp Business Platform services to other businesses, either by providing these services on their own, or by [partnering with a Solution Partner](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/multi-partner-solutions) who already offers these services.
Unlike Solution Partners, however, Tech Providers do not have credit lines. Instead, clients onboarded by Tech Providers must provide their own payment method after onboarding is complete. Meta will then bill these clients for API usage, and the Tech Provider will bill for other services.

title: Meta Tech Provider vs Tech Partner vs Solution Partner: What Each Tier Means for Your WhatsApp API
snippet:
Tech Partner is the upgrade once your app averages 2,500 messages or 200 calls a day and has at least 10 active clients, and it adds Meta Business Partner benefits such as training, analytics reports, and client matching.

businesses, and the tier your provider holds decides who sends you the bill for WhatsApp usage.[1]
- **Solution Partner:** a partner Meta has vetted, offering the full range of WhatsApp Business Platform services with a credit line, an arrangement in which the partner pays Meta for its clients’ usage and invoices them.
- **Tech Provider:** a company offering the same services, alone or with a Solution Partner, without a credit line, so clients add their own payment method, Meta bills them for API usage (the messages their software sends through WhatsApp), and the Tech Provider bills for its other services.
- **Tech Partner:** a Tech Provider that is, or is eligible to become, a “Meta Business Partner”, one of the companies Meta has vetted for technical skills and services.[2]

| | Solution Partner | Tech Provider | Tech Partner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full WhatsApp Business Platform services | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Credit line | Yes | No | No |
| Clients skip payment method collection | Yes | No | No |
| Bills clients directly for API usage | Yes | No (Meta bills the client) | No (Meta bills the client) |
| Is a “Meta Business Partner” | Yes | No | Yes |
| Accelerator program eligibility | Yes | No | Yes |
| Direct Support from Meta | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Embedded Signup, Meta’s in-product sign-up flow | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Starts WhatsApp Business account creation for a client | Yes | No | No |
| Partner-led business verification | Select Solution and Premier Solution Partners only | No | No |
| Access tokens (credentials sent with API calls) | Business tokens; system token only when sharing the credit line | Business tokens only | Business tokens only |
